walkthroughs.body_html:
Issues & Impact — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Issues & Impact brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Issues & Impact.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: Only the inner columns of each table.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
All rows from both tables combined.
Only rows with matching values in both tables.

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.
Only the inner columns of each table.

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: It is faster than symmetric encryption.
Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
It is impossible to break.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Pseudocode”?
options: A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Flowchart”?
options: A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
